we propose a smart mining method that allows for fast and accurate training of triplet models and we show that the proposed method achieves state of the art results for CUB200-2011 and Cars-196 datasets

we present a novel deep metric model with a smart mining procedure and an adaptive controller that achieves state of the art results for the CUB 200-2011 and Cars 196 datasets, and outperforms other mining methods for the CUB200-2011 dataset.

we propose an efficient mining method that produces effective training triplets for a low computational overhead and that we show empirically the effectiveness of this method for the CUB200-2011 and Cars 196 datasets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new mining method for deep metric learning that allows for a faster and more effective training of triplet models.
the problem of training deep metric learning models.
the development of a new deep metric learning method for producing feature embeddings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method allows for the fast training of deep metric learning models with high accuracy.
the proposed method achieves state of the art results on two popular benchmark datasets, and that it achieves this with significantly less computation than other competing mining techniques.
our approach is the first to achieve a new state of the-art on both CUB and Cars datasets while also being the fastest method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel method for mining hard negatives and positives for deep metric learning.
we propose a smart mining procedure for triplet deep metric learning, and we show empirically that this method allows for fast training convergence and state of the art performance.
the proposed smart mining procedure allows for a more efficient training of the triplet model and that the adaptive controller allows for a more effective convergence of the training.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed smart mining strategy can produce effective triplet samples for deep metric learning with low computational requirements.
smart mining methods can produce effective training samples at a lower computational cost than hard mining methods.
we show that the combination of smart mining and adaptive controllers is effective for training deep metric learning models.
